title: Protoplanetary Disk Properties in the Orion Nebula Cluster: Initial Results from Deep, High-resolution ALMA Observations
question: What are the sub-mm continuum fluxes, dust masses and sizes of protoplanetary disks in the dense Orion Nebula Cluster, and how do they depend on stellar mass and distance from theta1 Ori C compared with low-density regions?

data.sensitivity: rms ~0.1 mJy in clean regions, up to 2.5 mJy in BN/KL

evidence.quote: positions of HST-detected proplyds (cite: RRS08) and near-IR detected sources (cite: HC00; EISNER+16)
We used previous observations of the ONC at cm wavelengths (cite: FELLI+93a; FELLI+93b; ZAPATA+04; FORBICH+07; FORBRICH+16; SHEEHAN+16)

external_data.citation: (cite: FELLI+93a; FELLI+93b; ZAPATA+04; FORBICH+07; FORBRICH+16; SHEEHAN+16)

evidence.loc: Disk Properties as a function of Stellar Mass
evidence.quote: Stellar masses, determined spectroscopically, are available in the literature for about 60% of our ALMA-detected sample (cite: HILLENBRAND97; LUHMAN+00; SLESNICK+04; HILLENBRAND+13; INGRAHAM+14).

external_data.citation: Hillenbrand97; Luhman+00; Slesnick+04; Hillenbrand+13; Ingraham+14; Fang et al. in prep

what.value: Disk masses, sizes of other regions for comparison

evidence.quote: Mass distributions, computed in the same way, are available for Taurus (cite: ANDREWS+13), Lupus (cite: ANSDELL+16), Cham I (cite: PASCUCCI+16)

external_data.citation: Andrews+13; Ansdell+16; Pascucci+16; Ansdell+17; Barenfeld+16; Tripathi+17; Tazzari+17

recipe.method: tclean with multiscale clean, uv cut of 100 klambda, self-calibration, primary beam correction
Match to optical/near-IR positions within 0.5", detection threshold 4 sigma of local noise
Fit model of thick+thin free-free plus beta=1 dust to cm-to-sub-mm photometry for 52 sources
key_parameters: free parameters: turnover wavelength, free-free and dust fluxes at ALMA wavelength

recipe.method: 2D elliptical Gaussian fit to each source, beam-deconvolved; HWHM of major axis
Optically thin isothermal formula M = S d^2/(kappa B(T))
assumptions: d=400 pc, T_dust=20 K, beta=1, kappa0=2 cm2/g at 1.3 mm

recipe.goal: Test mass estimates with radiative transfer
recipe.method: RADMC-3D models with Rc=25 AU, flaring H/R ∝ R^0.15, Sigma ∝ R^-1, M-star L=0.5 Lsun, Teff=3500 K, grains 0.05-10000 um slope -3.5
Bayesian linear regression with upper limits for size vs flux; flux vs stellar mass and distance from theta1 Ori C

evidence.quote: sub-mm continuum emission above the 4$\sigma$ level was seen towards 104 cluster members
We detected sub-mm continuum emission towards 48 of the known proplyds, a detection rate of $\sim 80\%$.
$65 \pm 10\%$ of proplyds have dusty disks, while $45 \pm 7\%$ of all cluster members in the region have dusty disks.
12 are consistent with 100% of the sub-mm continuum flux arising from free-free emission.
the fluxes detected from dusty disks correspond to dust masses ranging from 0.5 to 80 Earth masses.

answer_key.quantity: Average dust temperature of compact disks (RT models)

evidence.quote: As shown in Figure [13](#fig:comprt), 40 K is more appropriate.
the gravitational radius is $\sim 20$ AU, similar to the disk radii inferred for our sample.
